title: Ed May's decision augmentation theory

tellings.quote: decision augmentation uh that pre pre the the researchers precognition is drawing them to start an experiment

plain: The writer Eric Wargo describes a theory from the psychic researcher Ed May called decision augmentation. It holds that good results in psychic experiments come from the researchers' own ability to sense the future, which nudges them to start an experiment at just the right moment. Wargo sums it up himself, and if true it would mean precognition, or knowing the future, quietly shapes the experiments meant to test it.
